answer: Random transcript audit works like a tide pulling back to expose hidden stones: each epoch the chain selects one prior answer, issues a fresh 256-bit nonce, and asks the author to re-derive its reasoning live. Any ripple between the replayed derivation and the stored transcript flags the identity. A single mismatch moves that account to a knoll of manual review, freezing its emissions until a human clears it. Covering 8000 fake identities costs roughly 190000 tokens and 35 operator hours per audit cycle, so sustained Sybil swarms drown in recurring replay cost.
